fields.reasoning: Read daemonPoll1 in internal/api/daemon.go: the 10-15 s cost is planRead and openCtxWorkspace, which re-read and fold the whole log; everything that depends on the clock or process liveness (Resumable with rs.Live and ctx.Now, daemonHeld with grace and the 15-minute hold, Pick/Skips over run journals) is cheap computation over run journals plus the folded workspace. Caching only the fold-derived inputs keyed on the stamps the change set's intent names keeps every time- and liveness-driven pick correct without inventing time-bucketed invalidation, while removing the expensive part. Run journals are small and are where liveness and backoff live, so they stay read every poll rather than becoming a cache key. For measurement, wall-clock thresholds are flaky on the shared VM and CI runners (test timings swing with load), so the test asserts the work skipped (fold count) rather than elapsed time, which is deterministic and directly proves the intent's 'skip the fold/pick work when unchanged'.
fields.statement: On a poll where the log, git refs and settings stamps are unchanged, the daemon skips only the fold-derived work: planRead (open reader, planGather, planCore), openCtxWorkspace (in daemonPoll1 and in the events pass daemonEvents), daemonCandidates, the change-set lookups (accepted state, ship Since, titles, has-leaves) and the lifecycle moves daemonEvents collects are reused from the last poll. The clock- and liveness-dependent steps run every poll against that cached result: rs.List of run journals, daemon.Resumable, daemonHeld (start grace, 15-minute unjournaled hold), resume backoff, disk check, autonomy stages, Pick/Skips, queued continues/starts, plan requests, the notify pass, and the event command for moves state does not list as handled. Any write the daemon itself makes (start, resume journal) invalidates the cache. A poll's cost is measured by a deterministic Go test, not wall-clock: build a repo with a large log and an event command, run the whole poll closure (daemonPoll1, daemonNotify, daemonEvents) twice with nothing changed, and assert through a fold counter hook that the second poll performs zero folds/plan reads, and that changing a stamp (new log entry, ref move, settings edit) makes the next poll fold again; an optional go benchmark reports ns/op for the unchanged poll but no test asserts a timing threshold.

fields.acceptance: A Go test in internal/api builds a repo with a large log (100+ change sets) and an event command set, runs the whole daemon poll closure (daemonPoll1, daemonNotify and daemonEvents) twice with nothing changed and asserts through the ctx.readLog counter that the second poll reads the log zero times across all three passes; the same test advances the clock past the 15-minute unjournaled hold with no stamp change and asserts the next poll picks the held change set again, and adds a log entry with a lifecycle move and asserts the next poll reads the log again and runs the event command for that move; a Go benchmark reports ns/op for the unchanged poll, and no test asserts a wall-clock threshold
fields.statement: A daemon poll where the log, git refs and daemon settings are unchanged since the last poll reuses that poll's folded workspace, plan result, candidates, change-set lookups and overlaps, and the lifecycle moves the events pass (daemonEvents) reads from the folded log, instead of re-reading and re-folding the log, while run journals, process liveness, clock-based holds, resume backoff, the disk check, picks, queued work, the notify pass and running the event command for moves not yet handled are still evaluated every poll
